A single observation at x=1/2 gives a 1×2 observation Jacobian, whose rank is at most one at every θ. At b=0 the state is even about the center and the slope sensitivity is odd, so the center has zero first derivative with respect to b. Moreover, reflection x↦1−x changes b to −b while preserving the central value. Opposite slope signs are observationally indistinguishable there. This is information lost by H, not a floating-point defect or merely stalled optimization.

Fits using center-only data and mirrored priors check that regularized estimates depend on prior choice. Obtaining a smooth stationary point or a positive regularized local curvature does not show that the data identified the slope sign. A penalty may select a solution by adding an assumption; it does not create the missing observational information.

A compact SVD of a 1×2 matrix returns only one singular value. Its lack of a second returned entry must not be read as absence of a null direction. We retain the zero direction and right singular vectors in the full two-dimensional parameter space. Five sensors and one central sensor are compared through independent sensitivities, not their counts alone.

Separate gradient, fitting, regularization and information checks

  1. Every adjoint component. Away from stationary points, perturb a and b separately in both directions and re-solve the primal equation for objective-only differences. Direct sensitivity gives another comparison. Include the explicit regularization term.
  2. Same-discretization two-parameter recovery. Compare multiple starts, accepted objective decrease, projected gradients and parameter errors while preserving the inverse-crime interpretation.
  3. Fixed reference observations and meshes. Refine the inverse mesh while keeping the numerical reference data fixed. Report reference-generation error checks; this is not an error against an exact continuous solution.
  4. One perturbation and a γ sweep. Hold observations and prior fixed while comparing fit residual, distance from the prior and parameter error.
  5. Insufficient observations. Check center-only rank, equality under slope reflection and prior dependence. Augmented rank is not data rank.

Measurement 1: both gradient components. On n=31, the points (a,b)=(1.3,−0.3),(2.1,0.2),(2.6,0.4) use γ=0,10⁻⁴,10⁻³ respectively. Across all six components, the largest absolute difference between the adjoint and central objective differences with ε=10⁻⁵ is about 7.74×10⁻¹². The direct-sensitivity difference is at most about 6.94×10⁻¹⁸. These checks do not rely on both gradients simply being small near an optimum.

Measurement 2: same-discretization recovery. For noiseless n=31 data, starts (1.3,−0.4),(2,0),(2.7,0.45) require 52,46,46 accepted updates. Their Euclidean errors against (2.2,0.35) are about 1.72×10⁻⁷,1.33×10⁻⁷,1.94×10⁻⁷, with final observation RMS below 6.5×10⁻⁹. All satisfy the unscaled projected-gradient infinity-norm threshold 10⁻⁹. This is a consistency control for the same discretization.

Measurement 3: inverse-mesh dependence for fixed numerical-reference data. Consecutive observation differences have Euclidean norms about 2.1046×10⁻⁶ for 255→511 and 5.2614×10⁻⁷ for 511→1023, a ratio about 4.00005. The n=1023 generator has an h²F infinity norm about 1.02×10⁻¹⁶, unscaled F Euclidean norm about 1.104×10⁻⁹ and final Newton correction infinity norm about 3.45×10⁻¹⁵. Its tolerances are 2×10⁻¹⁴ for h²F and 2×10⁻¹³ for the correction. Differently scaled residuals are not judged against the same tolerance. Self-refinement is an error diagnostic, not a rigorous error bound.

Holding those n=1023 observations fixed, inverse grids n=15,31,63,127 give generating-parameter errors about 2.2187×10⁻³,5.5382×10⁻⁴,1.3798×10⁻⁴,3.4049×10⁻⁵. Observed orders are about 2.0022,2.0049,2.0188; the final value is also affected by the fixed reference-grid floor. The n=127 estimate is about (2.1999715336,0.3499813181). It is not claimed to equal the estimate for exact continuous observations.

Measurement 4: stabilization and prior bias. On n=63 with prior (2,0) and one fixed observation perturbation, γ=0,10⁻⁵,10⁻⁴,10⁻³ are compared. The unregularized estimate is about (2.1995554520,0.3363439565), while γ=10⁻³ gives about (2.1937407950,0.0795027282). Generating-parameter errors increase through approximately 0.013663,0.024173,0.095712,0.270570. Observation RMS increases from about 6.7849×10⁻⁴ to 4.7026×10⁻³, while distance from the prior decreases from about 0.39109 to 0.20942.

At fixed γ, the norm of “perturbed-data estimate minus unperturbed-data estimate” decreases from about 0.013584 at γ=0 to 0.0032396 at γ=10⁻³. For this prior, reducing perturbation response and reducing generating-parameter error are different goals. The four perturbed fits agree with the objective-only simplex reference within 1.42×10⁻⁷ in parameter Euclidean norm. This is a local cross-check, not a rigorous error bound against an unknown exact optimum.

Measurement 5: data rank and regularized curvature. At n=31, θ=(2.2,0.35), five sensors with weights 1/5 give data singular values about (0.1728295,0.0175934), rank two and condition number about 9.8235. At the same θ, one central observation with weight one gives about (0.2500373,0), rank one. Different weights mean the leading singular-value magnitudes should not be directly compared.

The plotted central symmetric-state comparison uses a separate diagnostic point θ=(2.2,0), one central observation with weight one and γ=10⁻². Its data-only singular values are about (0.2499068,0), while augmented values are about (0.2691718,0.1). Data rank remains one; the extra curvature comes from the penalty.

Measurement 6: central observations and mirrored priors. At n=31 with fixed center-only reference data and γ=10⁻⁴, the same initial vector (2,0) with priors (2.2,±0.4) leads after 101 updates to estimates about (2.19930979,±0.39998726). Both have observation RMS about 2.7818×10⁻⁷, so the data do not distinguish the opposite slope signs. Separately, central predictions generated at θ=(2.2,±0.35) differ by about 1.94×10⁻¹⁵. These results match the observation operator’s reflection symmetry.

Distinguish why an estimate moves and what was verified

Generating-parameter error, observation fit, primal residual, adjoint residual and projected gradient measure different things. Regularization, fixed observation perturbations, inverse discretization and reference-generation errors can shift a fully converged fit away from θ*. Conversely, a small data residual does not establish that both parameters were identified.

Scope is a small dense-matrix example with two fixed coefficient basis functions, box bounds, the smaller-solution branch, known boundary conditions and observation operator, and synthetic data. General function recovery for λ(x), guarantees for many coefficients, BFGS or Gauss–Newton optimization, real measurements, unknown boundaries or model discrepancy, optimal experimental design and probabilistic uncertainty or confidence intervals are outside the checks.

Reference and validation scope

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Homogeneous, equal masses, isotropic scattering and constant collision rate. Each round randomly matches every particle once. Two initial beams at ±sqrt(3) give target temperature one. Each seed has zero total momentum and fixed total energy: its finite-N equilibrium is microcanonical, while Maxwell/Gamma are large-N references.

Adopted numerical method

Preserve pair center-of-mass velocity and relative speed, then choose the new relative direction uniformly on the sphere. Rounds count collision operations and are not calibrated physical time. For D=<vx²−(vy²+vz²)/2>, averaging a random partner multiplies the center-of-mass anisotropy by (N−2)/(2(N−1)); isotropic postcollision relative directions contribute zero expected anisotropy.

Editorial clarification

The adopted GLM uses ch=3 and damping rate kappa=0.18 ch n, with n cells per axis: damping is grid dependent. Both use the same continuous initial field, final time and CFL, while actual step counts and native div B operators differ.

Adopted numerical method

Reuse the published first-order Rusanov/forward-Euler solvers: shared corner-EMF discrete curl for CT and cell-centered hyperbolic/parabolic GLM cleaning. Independent Athena++ uses HLLD, PLM and RK2.

∇⋅B=0,Bt+∇×E=0\nabla\cdot\mathbf B=0,\qquad \mathbf B_t+\nabla\times\mathbf E=0∇⋅B=0,Bt​+∇×E=0

Verification limits and failures

Face CT divergence and centered GLM divergence use different operators; common cell-centered diagnostics are also reported. Athena initializes face-averaged magnetic fields by differencing a vector potential, so comparison includes discretization differences of identical continuous data. This is a short planar test, not validation of shocks, 3D, UCT or CTU.

Verification limits and failures

A bath diagnostic, not another independent physical problem. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. Statistical decisions apply to fixed seeds/budgets, not general mixing guarantees.

Reference and validation scope

Check canonical Gaussian/Gamma distributions and K/U/H means/variances. For finite steps, compare the Verlet-shadow position variance T/[omega²(1−h² omega²/4)] and momentum variance T against a separately constructed Lyapunov solution. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Assumptions, units and boundaries

m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), Nf=2. tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05. Evolve 8192 canonically initialized replicas and a separate 4096-replica ensemble with q,p scaled by 1.4 to t=20. Correlation lags are 0/0.5/1/2/4.

Check canonical Gaussian/Gamma distributions and K/U/H means/variances. For finite steps, compare the Verlet-shadow position variance T/[omega²(1−h² omega²/4)] and momentum variance T against a separately constructed Lyapunov solution. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Check Langevin q,p,K,H correlations against independent discrete propagation; report CSVR correlations with independent-replica standard errors and tau/h dependence.

Verification limits and failures

Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD.

    Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-theory-and-appendix

    Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-equations-and-algorithm

    Checked sections I–II, finite-step update Eq. (8), the sign of alpha in Eq. (9) using the same Gaussian, the Nf=1 Langevin limit and tau=1/(2 gamma). The original long Lennard-Jones transport calculations are not reproduced.

  3. Giovanni Bussi (2026). Research algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling

    Review scope / review_level: author-official-algorithm-note

Assumptions, units and boundaries

m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), lambda=0.2, U=sum(omega²q²/2+lambda q⁴/4). Use 8192 canonical and 4096 heated replicas, t=20, tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05, lags 0/0.5/1/2/4.

References and measured quantities

Obtain coordinate normalizers/CDFs and U moments by 1D quadrature, and the H CDF by convolving exponential K with the 2D positional Boltzmann density. Save the difference between quadrature tolerances 2e−10 and 2e−12; a separate rejection ensemble also checks H. Verification limits and failures

A small example for one separable two-mode quartic potential and fixed seeds. H is not treated as harmonic Gamma. No independent exact full-system dynamical reference is claimed, and neither matching correlations nor time order hidden by sampling noise is an acceptance claim. Molecular transport, quantum and ab initio MD are outside scope.

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

    Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-theory-and-appendix

    Checked sections I–II, finite-step update Eq. (8), the sign of alpha in Eq. (9) using the same Gaussian, the Nf=1 Langevin limit and tau=1/(2 gamma). The original long Lennard-Jones transport calculations are not reproduced.

validation-biology.title: Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation
validation-biology.html:
Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation

Follow a 1D periodic Schnakenberg system from finite-amplitude transients to post-growth patterns. Compare with a separate numerical reference and distinguish grid, time-step and reference errors.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-biology-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

Finite-amplitude Schnakenberg transient: nonlinearity and independent reference

Validate a finite-amplitude reaction-diffusion transient to t=8 with an independent Fourier–Galerkin reference, grid/time convergence and newly generated harmonics.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Centered spatial difference
  • Implicit midpoint

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. FFT does not change FD space into spectral space. Fail on nonconvergence/budget excess; never clip concentrations.

No corresponding equation-registry entry is registered. The example-specific definition above supplies its formulation, approximation or diagnostic.

Problem figure

A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

Turing instability: linear growth and small-amplitude patterns

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.

No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

Assumptions, units and boundaries

1D periodic x∈[0,2π), a=.1,b=.9,D=(.01,1). Common IC u=1+.08cos(2x)+.01cos(4x), v=.9−.03cos(2x)−.002cos(4x), restricted to a reflection-even, pi-periodic invariant subspace with a fixed origin.

Editorial clarification

Space refinement uses a separate Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference; time refinement uses an independently integrated Radau solution of the same FD semidiscrete system, not an exact continuous-PDE solution. Splitting error masked spatial error in the first coarse-step pilot. Steps were refined while keeping the acceptance criteria; the original input and failed metrics remain in the release.

Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

  1. A. M. Turing (1952). The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis · DOI: 10.1098/rstb.1952.0012

    Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-sections

    Checked the university-hosted original scan, sections 6–7 (printed pp.46–50), ring formulation/linearization and bibliography. Distinct from the adopted coefficients, finite-amplitude reference and mature shape.

  2. J. Schnakenberg (1979). Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour · DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(79)90042-0

    Review scope / review_level: official-bibliography-and-publisher-indexed-abstract

    Checked official PubMed bibliography/DOI and publisher-indexed abstract. Full text returned403. Historical source for the reaction family, not a claim to reproduce original coefficients or experiments.

  3. G. Strang (1968). On the Construction and Comparison of Difference Schemes · DOI: 10.1137/0705041

    Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-nonlinear-composition

    Checked original pp.510–512 for half-step composition and nonlinear second-order construction. This does not guarantee positivity or accuracy at arbitrary steps in the adopted model.

  4. E. Hairer (2010). Geometric Numerical Integration, Lecture2

    Review scope / review_level: author-lecture-selected-midpoint-and-splitting

    Checked theorem3 and section5 of the author-hosted lecture for implicit-midpoint formula/order and symmetric splitting. Hamiltonian symplectic claims are not transferred to this chemical model.

  5. The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp and Radau reference

    Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-api-specification

    Checked official Radau IIA order5, local rtol/atol scaling, analytic Jacobians and termination status. ODE tolerances do not certify global continuum-PDE accuracy.

Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics

Compare local trapping and between-mode movement on a bimodal target. Check autocorrelation, effective sample size and convergence diagnostics against an independent implementation, and expose missed exploration that diagnostics alone cannot detect.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-mcmc-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory.

Compare dispersed local MH, same-mode local MH and symmetry-informed reflection/local MH on the same bimodal target. Separate detecting expected mixing failures from successful finite-budget mode exploration.

Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value.

No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Dimensionless1D target p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1), mean0/variance37/positive occupancy.5. Three fixed seeds, four chains,1024 warmup and16384 retained draws/chain. Prefixes1024/4096/16384 are nested, not independent replications. Rejections/self-transitions are retained.

Editorial clarification

Passing this validation means confirming the well-mixing run and correctly exposing failures and diagnostic blind spots in deliberately trapped runs; it does not mean every run converged. Rhat and ESS depend on the observable, finite sample and initial states, and can look reassuring when all chains miss the same mode. Reflection jumps exploit known target symmetry for this comparison and do not guarantee exploration of arbitrary unknown multimodal targets.

Adopted numerical method

Local scale.8; mixed uses y=−x+.8Z with probability.1, otherwise y=x+.8Z. The state-independent mixture is symmetric q(y|x)=q(x|y), so MH uses the log-target ratio. Chains use independent PCG64 streams, with no adaptation or removal of rejected states.

Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. Verification limits and failures

An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations.

Verification limits and failures

An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations. ArviZ raw constant-ESS=N is not evidence of mixing. Globally identical values yield null/status; differing per-chain constants yield null/infinite-separation Rhat while retaining raw huge-finite/infinite library values outside ordinary finite comparisons. Bulk ESS is not a raw-mean MCSE estimator.

Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

  1. A. Vehtari, A. Gelman, D. Simpson, B. Carpenter and P.-C. Bürkner (2021). Rank-Normalization, Folding, and Localization: An Improved R-hat for Assessing Convergence of MCMC (with Discussion) · DOI: 10.1214/20-BA1221

    Review scope / review_level: corrected-author-paper-selected-sections

    Checked original sections3–4, the2021-06-22 correction of Eq4.1 to denominator S+1/4, and the constant-indicator warning. This does not reproduce every original numerical experiment.

  2. C. J. Geyer (1992). Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011137

    Review scope / review_level: original-selected-paired-sequence-theory

    Checked section3.3 and Theorems3.1/3.2 for reversibility assumptions and initial-positive/monotone sequences. Main article pp473–483 are distinguished from combined discussion pagination; no claim gives exact true ESS from finite chains.

  3. A. Gelman and D. B. Rubin (1992). Inference from Iterative Simulation Using Multiple Sequences · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011136

    Review scope / review_level: original-selected-multiple-chain-starting-points

    Checked the original introduction/section2 on multiple sequences and overdispersed starts. Distinct from the later rank/folded method, and not a reproduction of every1992 finite-sample correction.

  4. The ArviZ developers (2024). ArviZ0.20.0 public diagnostics API and tagged source

    Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-source-and-actual-independent-execution

    Checked the official0.20.0 rhat/ess API and tagged source for splitting, ranks, Type7 quantiles, endpoints and constant conventions. validation-mhd-convergence.html:
CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence

Compare CT and GLM discretizations with a matched flux family, LLF coefficient, time steps and fixed physical damping. Use a constructed smooth exact solution and independent Athena++ results to separate spatial, time-integration and reference differences.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-mhd-convergence-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

CT and GLM: mesh/time convergence of a moving magnetostatic equilibrium

Use a constructed exact equilibrium with nonzero magnetic force balanced by a pressure gradient, matching CT/GLM initial cell states, flux speed bound and time-step sequence.

Reference and validation scope

Measure conserved-variable L1/L2/Linf errors and observed orders at16²/32²/64². Compare finest-grid step doubling with.1 of the spatial error. Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Periodic unit square, gamma5/3, mu0=1, planar MHD. A=.05[cos2pi(x−.3t)+cos2pi(y−.2t)], B=(Ay,−Ax), rho1, v=(.3,.2), p=.1+(2pi)²A²/2 at t=.1. Compare analytic conserved cell averages. This is a constructed verification case, not a claimed published standard benchmark.

Editorial clarification

This translating smooth equilibrium is an exact solution constructed for the Atlas. Compare conserved cell averages, distinguishing pressure recovered from them from the exact cell average of pressure. A separate time integrator on the same spatial semidiscretization checks time error; it is not an independent PDE solver.

Adopted numerical method

Both use piecewise constants, the same fixed Rusanov speed alpha3 and forward Euler. CT uses face B/shared arithmetic corner EMFs; GLM uses cell B/psi with fixed ch3 and physical damping rate kappa2. All meshes use384 steps and identical CT/GLM dt sequences; initial reconstructed CT cell B matches GLM cell B.

Measure conserved-variable L1/L2/Linf errors and observed orders at16²/32²/64². Compare finest-grid step doubling with.1 of the spatial error. At fixed8², compare16/32/64/128 steps with doubly refined DOP853 tolerances/max steps. Record mass/E, positivity, native CT divergence, common cell divergence and psi.

Verification limits and failures

With constant LLF viscosity and periodic centered operators, the GLM div=psi=0 subspace remains invariant up to roundoff. This tests coupled-MHD accuracy; a separate nonphysical control activates cleaning. p(q-average) is not the exact averaged p. DOP853 is independent in time only and shares the spatial RHS. Step differences are empirical contamination indicators, not rigorous bounds; face/cell representation differences remain part of the comparison.

This diagnostic deliberately violates the divergence constraint while giving both methods the same initial cell magnetic field. operator-splitting.html:
Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang

Operator splitting advances separate parts of an evolution equation and composes their solution maps. Lie–Trotter uses two full substeps; Strang surrounds one full substep with two half substeps. Even exact subproblem solutions leave a composition error when their order matters.

Run both on the same reaction–diffusion input: a 32-point, T=1 Schnakenberg system with matched initial fields, subsolvers and observation times. Four step sizes measure first-order Lie–Trotter and second-order Strang. Unsplit Radau/DOP853 references use the same FD semidiscretization; this is separate from spatial convergence and exact continuum solutions.

Fixed input, results, code and the 16-test rerun receipt

Split the evolution, define one time step

u˙=F(u)+G(u),v˙=F(v) ⇒ φFh,w˙=G(w) ⇒ φGh.\dot u=F(u)+G(u),\qquad \dot v=F(v)\ \Rightarrow\ \varphi_F^h,\qquad \dot w=G(w)\ \Rightarrow\ \varphi_G^h.u˙=F(u)+G(u),v˙=F(v) ⇒ φFh​,w˙=G(w) ⇒ φGh​.

Start with a sufficiently smooth autonomous finite-dimensional initial-value problem. Each φ is the exact flow of its subproblem, and h is one step for the summed equation. Compositions act from right to left. Advancing F for h and then G for h approximates one step of length h for the original equation, not 2h. Using only h/2 for each part would instead halve the leading vector field.

The approach uses tractable subproblems such as reaction and diffusion, transport and sources, or drift and force in a separable Hamiltonian. Splitting is a separate choice from spatial discretization and physical modeling. Matrix exponentials below apply to the linear specialization F(u)=Au, G(u)=Bu.

Lie–Trotter: two ordered full substeps

un+1=Lh(un)=(φGh∘φFh)(un),Lh=ehBehA(u˙=(A+B)u).u^{n+1}=L_h(u^n)=(\varphi_G^h\circ\varphi_F^h)(u^n),\qquad L_h=e^{hB}e^{hA}\quad(\dot u=(A+B)u).un+1=Lh​(un)=(φGh​∘φFh​)(un),Lh​=ehBehA(u˙=(A+B)u).

Our convention applies F first and G to the updated state. Reversing the order gives another first-order method, generally with a different value. Computing both substeps independently from the old state and adding their increments is a different update.

ehBehA−eh(A+B)=h22(BA−AB)+O(h3),[A,B]=AB−BA.e^{hB}e^{hA}-e^{h(A+B)}=\frac{h^2}{2}(BA-AB)+O(h^3),\qquad [A,B]=AB-BA.ehBehA−eh(A+B)=2h2​(BA−AB)+O(h3),[A,B]=AB−BA.

Expand both exponentials through h²: the commutator remains in the difference from the exact summed flow. Its sign here follows the chosen product and reverses with the substep order. The local defect means the one-step difference starting from an exact state: O(h²). Under stability and smoothness, accumulated error at a fixed final time is O(h). The product limit and a finite-step error estimate are separate statements.

Strang: a symmetric second-order composition

un+1=Sh(un)=(φFh/2∘φGh∘φFh/2)(un),Sh=ehA/2ehBehA/2.u^{n+1}=S_h(u^n)=(\varphi_F^{h/2}\circ\varphi_G^h\circ\varphi_F^{h/2})(u^n),\qquad S_h=e^{hA/2}e^{hB}e^{hA/2}.un+1=Sh​(un)=(φFh/2​∘φGh​∘φFh/2​)(un),Sh​=ehA/2ehBehA/2.

Apply a half F step, a full G step and another half F step, each to the current state. G/2→F→G/2 is another valid Strang variant. The two variants generally produce different numerical solutions and error constants.

S−h=Sh−1,Sh−eh(A+B)=O(h3),[A,B]=0 ⇒ Lh=Sh=eh(A+B).S_{-h}=S_h^{-1},\qquad S_h-e^{h(A+B)}=O(h^3),\qquad [A,B]=0\ \Rightarrow\ L_h=S_h=e^{h(A+B)}.S−h​=Sh−1​,Sh​−eh(A+B)=O(h3),[A,B]=0 ⇒ Lh​=Sh​=eh(A+B).

When inverse flows exist, replacing h by −h reverses the symmetric composition. Expansion through the quadratic term cancels the leading Lie–Trotter defect, leaving local O(h³) and global O(h²) errors; nested commutators enter the next error terms. For commuting finite matrices, both exact-subflow compositions equal the exact summed flow. Extending this statement to unbounded PDE operators requires domain and regularity conditions.

A standalone Strang step calls one additional subflow. Over consecutive constant steps, adjacent half F steps can be merged when the exact flow has the group property (a positive-time semigroup suffices for diffusion). Lie–Trotter uses 2N subflow calls and merged Strang 2N+1. Actual work depends on each subproblem, output and boundary processing, and whether numerical subflows permit merging. Call counts are not measured runtimes.

This is a two-component harmonic oscillator with nondimensional q, p and time. Its subflows require only addition and multiplication; the reference is the analytic sine/cosine solution. The first-step formulas already expose the local defect orders. Use the norm of both components to avoid mistaking componentwise cancellation for higher order. A separate single-step check from the exact initial state gives local orders near 2 and 3. Conditions: order and stability can be lost

The stated orders assume a smooth solution, sufficiently small steps, a fixed finite interval and suitable stability. Shocks, stiff relaxation and nonsmooth initial data can invalidate those expectations. PDE subproblems and their stages need compatible boundary data. Check order reduction from inhomogeneous or time-dependent boundaries separately from spatial and nonlinear-solver errors.

A symmetric arrangement alone does not make approximate subflows second order. Standard Strang composition needs subsolvers with at least second-order consistency and sufficiently tight iteration tolerances to retain second order. Exact or symmetric subsolvers are needed to retain time symmetry as well. Direct substitution of forward or backward Euler generally reduces the order to one. Nonautonomous problems require a suitable extended system including time, or consistent subproblem time arguments; freezing everything at the old time is not enough.

det⁡Lh=det⁡Sh=1,tr⁡Lh=tr⁡Sh=2−h2,0<∣h∣<2(oscillator).\det L_h=\det S_h=1,\quad\operatorname{tr}L_h=\operatorname{tr}S_h=2-h^2,\quad 0<|h|<2\quad\text{(oscillator)}.detLh​=detSh​=1,trLh​=trSh​=2−h2,0<∣h∣<2(oscillator).

For this oscillator both update matrices have determinant 1 and trace 2−h², giving bounded oscillatory modes for 0<|h|<2. Exact subflows do not by themselves guarantee unconditional stability. Composition inherits only properties preserved by its submaps: Hamiltonian symplecticity does not imply positivity for arbitrary reactions or exact conservation of the full energy.

Existing Strang examples and the distinction from IMEX

The existing reaction–diffusion finite-amplitude Schnakenberg and saturated-pattern examples use exact half steps of centered-difference diffusion and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step in a Strang composition. Their published records give spatial and temporal checks for those fixed conditions. They are separate from this oscillator illustration, and their distributions, tolerances and results are preserved.

IMEX also separates parts of the right-hand side, but IMEX time integration combines explicit and implicit stage equations, whereas the splitting here composes subproblem flows. These are different updates. For the separable-Hamiltonian connection, see symplectic integration.

Lightweight reproduction and publication scope

Python 3 standard libraries suffice to recompute the table, local defects, reversed ordering and commuting control. The script prints JSON; --check compares saved values. This fixed two-component reading illustration is not a general splitting-solver distribution or a new common execution-registry entry. The oscillator script remains a reading illustration. A separate dedicated lightweight reaction–diffusion release now executes both methods; their educational-code status is limited to that fixed input.

Lie–Trotter versus Strang on the same nonlinear reaction–diffusion input

Computation for a fixed target

Advance a 32-point Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion problem to T=1 with matched inputs and subsolvers. Four step sizes check first-/second-order temporal convergence, reference sensitivity, reaction balance and failure on nonconvergence in a lightweight comparison.

This measures temporal error of the adopted compositions at fixed space, including splitting and midpoint-reaction discretization errors. It is not an exact continuum solution, spatial convergence check or independent PDE-engine comparison. Reactions do not conserve u+v; positivity is observed only for the fixed input. Work is reported as actual subflow calls, without runtime rankings or universal Strang superiority. This additional comparison of the existing Schnakenberg problem changes neither physical-problem counts, the common 22 examples, old release criteria nor success history. Long-time patterns, 2D and general boundaries are outside scope.

Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Length 2pi, stationary unit-density ions, electron q/m=−1, plasma frequency one, sinusoidal displacement 0.001 and final time 1.6. Mesh runs retain 2048 particles; time runs retain a 32-cell mesh and 256 particles. The particle weight is w=2pi/N and n is the grid count.

Editorial clarification

DOP853 integrates the same particle-grid RHS and is independent only as a time algorithm. Separate quiet-start refinement from random-load noise at time zero; do not claim exact energy conservation.

Adopted numerical method

CIC deposition/matched gathering, spectral Poisson and velocity Verlet. The independent time algorithm DOP853 integrates the same particle-grid RHS; compare its own maximum-step refinements.

References and measured quantities

Refine 16/32/64 grids and dt=.2/.1/.05 separately; distinguish continuum cos(t) from time-reference errors. Record the real odd derivative’s Nyquist null mode separately from Gauss residuals. Compare time-zero CIC mode power at 64 seeds and N=256/1024/4096 with its analytic expectation.

Verification limits and failures

DOP853 is not an independent PIC spatial implementation. Distinguish charge/momentum preservation from approximate energy conservation. Initial-noise N scaling does not validate evolved warm plasmas. Landau damping, electromagnetic/relativistic PIC and collisions remain unvalidated.

Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Homogeneous equal-mass isotropic Maxwell collisions; N=16/64/256, 64 independent seeds, zero momentum and sum|v|²=3N. Start with two beams and run 24 collision rounds; rounds are not calibrated physical time.

Editorial clarification

Use the finite-N equilibrium beta law and independent sphere samples at fixed invariants. Account for particle correlation via independent-seed error; collision rounds are not calibrated time or hard-sphere transport.

Adopted numerical method

Uniform random complete matchings and isotropic pair scattering preserve pair momentum/energy. An independent sampler projects Gaussian vectors into the zero-center-of-mass subspace and fixes their radius.

References and measured quantities

Check maximum momentum/energy errors over all rounds against deterministic tolerances. Use independent-seed standard errors for six-round anisotropy, four energy-CDF points and fourth moments against the finite-N beta reference. Separate decreasing CDF sampling error with N from finite-N Maxwell bias.

Verification limits and failures

Statistical diagnostics cover fixed 64-seed ensembles, not every seed. Conservation correlates particles within a seed; do not use IID KS p-values. No spatial streaming, collision cells, speed-dependent hard-sphere selection or transport coefficients.

Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Steady uniform slab, optical depths .1/.7/3, unit incoming positive-hemisphere intensity, no reverse inflow/scattering/emission. Incoming photon directions for a flux estimator have density 2mu.

Editorial clarification

Separate space and angle errors for a pure-absorption slab, comparing characteristics, adaptive quadrature and photon survival. Finite-seed coverage is no all-seed guarantee; scattering and radiation hydrodynamics remain unvalidated.

Adopted numerical method

Use upstream finite volumes and Gauss-Legendre ordinates; exact exponential propagation removes spatial error in the angle series. Monte Carlo independently tracks survival/absorption using mu=sqrt(U) and exponential optical paths.

Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem

Compare short-time nonlinear Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion with the same initial field, grid, subsolvers and observation times. This lightweight addition checks temporal convergence and numerical-reference sensitivity while retaining existing spatial and long-time pattern records.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Lie–Trotter versus Strang on the same nonlinear reaction–diffusion input

Advance a 32-point Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion problem to T=1 with matched inputs and subsolvers. Four step sizes check first-/second-order temporal convergence, reference sensitivity, reaction balance and failure on nonconvergence in a lightweight comparison.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Lie–Trotter splitting
  • Strang splitting

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Lie–Trotter uses diffusion(h) then reaction(h); Strang uses diffusion(h/2), reaction(h), diffusion(h/2), always passing the updated state. Both apply the exact exponential of the centered-FD diffusion matrix by FFT and the same implicit-midpoint reaction/Newton tolerance 2e−13 with at most 12 residual evaluations. The reaction flow is a second-order approximation, not exact. No clipping, adaptive steps or fallback; nonconvergence is failure.

Turing instability: linear growth and small-amplitude patterns

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

The reference independently assembles the SAME FD semidiscretization with a real-space sparse matrix and separately written reaction RHS, then integrates it unsplit with Radau. Tighter Radau and separate DOP853 runs measure reference sensitivity relative to the finest Strang error. Norms are per-species mean L1, RMS L2 and maximum L∞, then the worse species; refinement uses the maximum across the four common positive observation times. Also record Newton-tolerance sensitivity, positive tested substeps, reaction source/sink balance and reversed-Lie ordering.

No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Nondimensional 1D periodic [0,2pi), N=32, a=.1, b=.9, D=(.01,1). The initial fields u₀=1+.08cos2x+.01cos4x and v₀=.9−.03cos2x−.002cos4x match the earlier finite-amplitude example. This new run ends at T=1, uses 16/32/64/128 steps and common output times 0/.25/.5/.75/1. The fixed input is reflection-even and pi-periodic.

Adopted numerical method

Lie–Trotter uses diffusion(h) then reaction(h); Strang uses diffusion(h/2), reaction(h), diffusion(h/2), always passing the updated state. Both apply the exact exponential of the centered-FD diffusion matrix by FFT and the same implicit-midpoint reaction/Newton tolerance 2e−13 with at most 12 residual evaluations. The reaction flow is a second-order approximation, not exact. No clipping, adaptive steps or fallback; nonconvergence is failure.

References and measured quantities

The reference independently assembles the SAME FD semidiscretization with a real-space sparse matrix and separately written reaction RHS, then integrates it unsplit with Radau. Tighter Radau and separate DOP853 runs measure reference sensitivity relative to the finest Strang error. Norms are per-species mean L1, RMS L2 and maximum L∞, then the worse species; refinement uses the maximum across the four common positive observation times. Also record Newton-tolerance sensitivity, positive tested substeps, reaction source/sink balance and reversed-Lie ordering.

Verification limits and failures

This measures temporal error of the adopted compositions at fixed space, including splitting and midpoint-reaction discretization errors. It is not an exact continuum solution, spatial convergence check or independent PDE-engine comparison. Reactions do not conserve u+v; positivity is observed only for the fixed input. Work is reported as actual subflow calls, without runtime rankings or universal Strang superiority. This additional comparison of the existing Schnakenberg problem changes neither physical-problem counts, the common 22 examples, old release criteria nor success history. Long-time patterns, 2D and general boundaries are outside scope.

Noh shocks: zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical flow

An original small 1D finite-volume code solves zero-pressure Noh flow in planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry. Grids 64/128/256/512 measure full-domain error, origin heating, shock location and budgets, and compare spherical boundary-inflow time-quadrature error with its analytic identity.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Rusanov / local Lax–Friedrichs flux
  • Heun / SSPRK(2,2)
  • MUSCL reconstruction
  • Minmod

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Rusanov flux with SSPRK2 (Heun). Planar/cylindrical runs retain piecewise-constant reconstruction. Spherical runs reconstruct conserved variables linearly around volume centroids with minmod slopes based on centroid distances in interior cells and zero slopes in the two boundary cells. A single theta per cell scales all conserved slopes at both faces to check face density/internal energy. Cell means are never corrected and no pressure seed/floor is used. Wave speeds, Rusanov flux and numerical stress P*=F_mom-((u_L+u_R)/2)F_mass use the same face states. The geometric CFL V/(A_La_L+A_Ra_R) uses the prescribed .35. Spherical source quadrature exactly integrates the face-linear numerical stress against 2r dr; planar/cylindrical runs keep the old arithmetic rule. Reconstructed reflection faces use even/odd parity, with physical cold inflow at the outer face. Every RK stage is checked and invalid states cause a retained failure.

  • Compressible Euler equations

    The scoped planar, cylindrical-radial and spherical-radial forms of ideal-gas Euler. This example defines the geometric source, outer inflow and exactly zero initial pressure in its formulas and fixed input.

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Retain the planar/cylindrical acceptance file and all 59 original decisions, and save spherical criteria, inputs and source hashes before the first spherical PDE run. The initial cylindrical failure retains its source, all eight diagnostic logs and failed summary; the face-stress revision was tested against the same gates. Analytic conserved means split shock-crossing integrals and distinguish p(mean U) from mean p. The pinned independent LANL ExactPack analytic comparison includes d=1/2/3. New spherical PDE refinements separately measure full-domain r^2-weighted L1/L2/Linf, density L1 in r<=.70rs including the origin, and center/shock/plateau diagnostics. Discrete stage-weighted inflow budgets are distinct from continuous analytic totals; SSPRK2 boundary quadrature is checked through M_h-M_exact=sum(dt^3)/6 and E_h-E_exact=sum(dt^3)/12. The first spherical run retained arithmetic source quadrature and failed two of 105 gates (finest shock-position error 3.923 cells, plateau-density error 11.03%); all results are retained. A second attempt changed only spherical stress quadrature, but still failed the same two gates (3.919 cells and 11.018% density error). A third attempt retains that quadrature and adds MUSCL/minmod reconstruction only for spherical runs, against the same 105 criteria. The third attempt completed 28 tests and all 12 grid runs, passing all 105 gates. At spherical N=512 the whole-domain density L1 is .0114343, shock error 1.98856 cells, plateau-density error 5.2533%, and origin-inclusive core-density L1 .0549503. Maximum center specific-internal-energy excess is 20.59%, worse than the second attempt's 15.52%; not every diagnostic improves.

Outer density is (1+t)^(d-1), the origin reflects, and the measure is r^(d-1)dr. The same angular factor is omitted throughout; spherical analytic totals are M=512/375 and E=256/375. Its figure is a central section of a 1D radial solution, not a Cartesian 2D/3D calculation or a test of angular symmetry breaking.

References and measured quantities

Retain the planar/cylindrical acceptance file and all 59 original decisions, and save spherical criteria, inputs and source hashes before the first spherical PDE run. The initial cylindrical failure retains its source, all eight diagnostic logs and failed summary; the face-stress revision was tested against the same gates. Analytic conserved means split shock-crossing integrals and distinguish p(mean U) from mean p. The pinned independent LANL ExactPack analytic comparison includes d=1/2/3. New spherical PDE refinements separately measure full-domain r^2-weighted L1/L2/Linf, density L1 in r<=.70rs including the origin, and center/shock/plateau diagnostics. Discrete stage-weighted inflow budgets are distinct from continuous analytic totals; SSPRK2 boundary quadrature is checked through M_h-M_exact=sum(dt^3)/6 and E_h-E_exact=sum(dt^3)/12. The first spherical run retained arithmetic source quadrature and failed two of 105 gates (finest shock-position error 3.923 cells, plateau-density error 11.03%); all results are retained. A second attempt changed only spherical stress quadrature, but still failed the same two gates (3.919 cells and 11.018% density error). A third attempt retains that quadrature and adds MUSCL/minmod reconstruction only for spherical runs, against the same 105 criteria. The third attempt completed 28 tests and all 12 grid runs, passing all 105 gates. At spherical N=512 the whole-domain density L1 is .0114343, shock error 1.98856 cells, plateau-density error 5.2533%, and origin-inclusive core-density L1 .0549503. Maximum center specific-internal-energy excess is 20.59%, worse than the second attempt's 15.52%; not every diagnostic improves.

Verification limits and failures

An educational calculation: first-order space in planar/cylindrical flow and MUSCL-type limited linear reconstruction in spherical flow. Origin heating and finite-grid plateau errors remain; the center is never removed from whole-domain error. Because r^2 weighting can make central defects appear small, an origin-inclusive fixed-core norm and enlarged view are also shown. Vanishing Linf/center maximum error, high order for the complete method on smooth spherical problems, general stage positivity with the geometric source, Cartesian multidimensional flow and independent arbitrary-gamma validation are not established. Cylindrical Linf was not monotone in the old series; spherical L2/Linf and heating are retained as diagnostics. Roundoff-scale discrete mass/energy balance coexists with O(dt^2) spherical boundary-time-quadrature error against analytic totals. Radial momentum has a geometric source and is not a conserved Cartesian momentum component. ExactPack independently implements the analytic evaluator, not another numerical PDE engine.

Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

Noh:2D Cartesian flow and grid orientation error

A small 2D Euler finite-volume calculation evolves density, both momenta and total energy over the full square. Three grids,32²/64²/128², measure Noh-reference errors, budgets and grid orientation effects. The picture shows the actual evolved 2D array.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Unsplit shared-face x/y piecewise-constant Rusanov fluxes and SSPRK2/Heun. CFL .35 uses (max a_x+max a_y)/dx. Cold physical outer fluxes are spatially integrated analytically and their affine time dependence is integrated at both Heun stages. Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Inputs/source/acceptance hashes are saved before execution. All 19 unit tests and 49 gates on three grids passed at the first attempt. Analytic density is integrated over cells by splitting shock-circle cuts and 64-point Gauss quadrature with x=rs sin(theta), checked against 128 points and analytic total mass; these are quadrature references, not closed-form exact cell means. At 128², full-square density L1=.09981, origin-inclusive core L1=.12231; shock errors are.968 axis cells and1.469 diagonal cells. Maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about 4.6e-15. D4 conserved parity and continuous rotational symmetry are measured separately.

    Noh cold-inflow shock: planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry

    Analytic reference for the same Noh problem.1D uses exact conserved-volume means;2D uses density means from shock-split Cartesian cell quadrature. Distinguish points/cell means and p(mean U)/mean p.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Nondimensional [-.5,.5]², gamma=5/3, rho0=1, inward speed 1, p0=0, T=.6, shock radius.2. Initial conserved states are cell-center cold samples, not exact initial momentum means. All four edges prescribe supersonic inflow rho=1+t/r and u=(-x/r,-y/r). No symmetry boundary, radial projection or geometric source.

Cold physical outer fluxes are spatially integrated analytically and their affine time dependence is integrated at both Heun stages. No cell repair, pressure floor/seed or hidden timestep retry; invalid stages retain raw arrays and fail.

References and measured quantities

Inputs/source/acceptance hashes are saved before execution. All 19 unit tests and 49 gates on three grids passed at the first attempt. Analytic density is integrated over cells by splitting shock-circle cuts and 64-point Gauss quadrature with x=rs sin(theta), checked against 128 points and analytic total mass; these are quadrature references, not closed-form exact cell means. At 128², full-square density L1=.09981, origin-inclusive core L1=.12231; shock errors are.968 axis cells and1.469 diagonal cells. Maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about 4.6e-15. D4 conserved parity and continuous rotational symmetry are measured separately.

Verification limits and failures

A first-order-space lightweight example retains origin heating and shock errors. Finest maximum center specific internal energy is still about 14% high. Axis/diagonal shock-radius difference is about .501dx and is not monotone over these grids. Roundoff-level D4 parity does not establish exact circular symmetry. General perturbation stability, displaced origins, rotated meshes, 3D Cartesian flow and high-order accuracy are unverified. Earlier planar/cylindrical/spherical 1D editions and gates remain unchanged.

validation-sedov.html:
Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation

A lightweight spherical-radial Euler finite-volume example deposits unit energy inside fixed radius0.03. Three grids of128/256/512 radial cells measure differences from a point-blast similarity reference and conservation budgets. The picture is a section display of1D spherical data, not a2D Cartesian calculation.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-sedov-2026-11-23-r2 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Rusanov / local Lax–Friedrichs flux
  • Heun / SSPRK(2,2)

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Piecewise-constant Rusanov fluxes on spherical shells with SSPRK2/Heun. The radial-momentum source p(A_right-A_left)/V is integrated at the same RK stages, with a stationary uniform-pressure balance test. CFL.4 uses the reciprocal maximum (|u|+c)/(V/(A_left+A_right)), comparing with the remaining interval before division. No pressure seed, floor, cell repair or hidden timestep retry; an invalid stage retains raw conserved values and history and fails.

  • Compressible Euler equations

    The one-dimensional spherical-radial ideal-gas Euler system. This example defines origin reflection, geometric source, finite-radius energy deposition and outer boundary in its fixed input.

Problem figure

A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

Sedov–Taylor point blast

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Original r1 passed22 tests and48 gates on Mac, but its public-ZIP Linux run failed when warnings-as-errors raised a cold-tail CFL overflow. Revision r2 uses the algebraically equivalent reciprocal maximum-rate evaluation while preserving the original inputs, reference and48 acceptance gates. A new r2-specific pre-execution hash contract precedes23 tests and all four calculations/48 gates passing with warnings as errors. Original sources, contract and actual Linux-failure evidence remain archived. The independent reference integrates the similarity ODE with DOP853, normalizes energy, uses a regular asymptote for xi<.001 and split shell quadrature at the shock. Orders16/32, core cutoff and ODE tolerance are checked separately. The unmodified pinned ExactPack evaluator was independently run at6001/12001 points and compared away from the center/jump with its preregistered5e-4 criterion. Beta=1.15166641793, Rs(.05)=.34746791233. Origin/shock-inclusive volume-weighted density L1 within r<=1.2Rs is.17257/.12785/.07458 and pressure L1 is.18148/.13939/.07615. Finest shock error is1.096 cells; maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about8.89e-16.

  • Same-problem reference · Semi-analytic reference

    Sedov–Taylor point blast: energy-normalized spherical similarity solution

    An energy-normalized spherical similarity reference. Numerical integration of similarity ODEs and shell quadrature make this semi-analytic, not closed-form exact cell means. Finite-radius deposition is distinct from the singular ideal point-blast initial data. At fixed finite deposition radius, comparison with the point-source similarity reference includes deposition-model discrepancy; its refinement slope is not a pure spatial order. Changing deposition radius on the same finest grid is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a complete separation of continuum deposition and PDE-discretization errors.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Nondimensional gamma=5/3, ambient density1, velocity0, pressure0, radius[0,1], deposited energy1, T=.05. Uniform thermal energy inside a sphere is assigned using exact cut-shell volumes. Deposition radius0.03 is shared by all three grids; a separate512-cell run uses0.015. The origin is reflecting and the outer boundary is outflow; actual boundary fluxes enter measured budgets.

Editorial clarification

Revisionr1 passed22 tests and four runs on Mac, but its public-ZIP Linux retry passed22 tests then failed in the -Werror main run when a CFL candidate ratio overflowed at tiny cold-tail wave speeds. Revisionr2 evaluates the same CFL condition as1/max(speed/width), avoiding intermediate overflow. Inputs/acceptance thresholds stay unchanged; retain the old release/failure and independently rerun23 tests and all fixed inputs from a new ZIP. Fixed-radius point-source comparison includes model discrepancy: its refinement slope is not a pure spatial order, and the radius comparison is sensitivity rather than complete deposition/PDE-error separation. Original Linux failure: https://github.com/hrkoyama/hrkoyama.github.io/actions/runs/45109504662 (all22 tests passed; the first128-cell,rdep.03 main calculation raised RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in divide before completion).

Adopted numerical method

Piecewise-constant Rusanov fluxes on spherical shells with SSPRK2/Heun. The radial-momentum source p(A_right-A_left)/V is integrated at the same RK stages, with a stationary uniform-pressure balance test. CFL.4 uses the reciprocal maximum (|u|+c)/(V/(A_left+A_right)), comparing with the remaining interval before division. No pressure seed, floor, cell repair or hidden timestep retry; an invalid stage retains raw conserved values and history and fails.

References and measured quantities

Original r1 passed22 tests and48 gates on Mac, but its public-ZIP Linux run failed when warnings-as-errors raised a cold-tail CFL overflow. Revision r2 uses the algebraically equivalent reciprocal maximum-rate evaluation while preserving the original inputs, reference and48 acceptance gates. A new r2-specific pre-execution hash contract precedes23 tests and all four calculations/48 gates passing with warnings as errors. Original sources, contract and actual Linux-failure evidence remain archived. The independent reference integrates the similarity ODE with DOP853, normalizes energy, uses a regular asymptote for xi<.001 and split shell quadrature at the shock. Orders16/32, core cutoff and ODE tolerance are checked separately. The unmodified pinned ExactPack evaluator was independently run at6001/12001 points and compared away from the center/jump with its preregistered5e-4 criterion. Beta=1.15166641793, Rs(.05)=.34746791233. Origin/shock-inclusive volume-weighted density L1 within r<=1.2Rs is.17257/.12785/.07458 and pressure L1 is.18148/.13939/.07615. Finest shock error is1.096 cells; maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about8.89e-16.

Verification limits and failures

A finite deposition sphere and an ideal point blast have different initial data; reported errors combine deposition-model and discretization effects. The refinement slope is not a pure spatial order. Halving the source radius at the same512 cells changes density by about.000451 and pressure by.000619, but point-reference errors become slightly worse; no improvement or point-source-limit proof is claimed. Pressure compares numerical p(mean conserved U) with reference mean physical pressure, distinct from p(mean reference U). Center values and maximum errors remain reported. The finest density peak is about2.918 versus the exact jump4. The cold-tail local-CFL overflow that caused the r1 Linux failure is avoided in r2 by the equivalent maximum inverse-rate evaluation, without suppressing warnings or adding a physical floor. The regular tiny-core continuation is approximate, and ExactPack point probes exclude xi<.15. Cartesian2D/3D, general perturbations/asymmetry and high-order accuracy are unverified.

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

CFL.4 uses the sum of directional maximum acoustic rates; the top boundary uses each actual RK stage time. No state floor, repair or hidden retry. Invalid stages retain raw arrays/history and fail.

Double Mach reflection

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

The original preregistered20 unit tests passed. Before the full three-grid run, read-only review added an absent-front diagnostic guard and one test; the old contract/source are preserved and a revision contract was frozen. All21 tests, three final-time runs and40 gates passed with-W error. Previously independently executed Ny64/128 primitive MUSCL/generalized-minmod theta1.5/HLL/Heun data from the RKDG kit are reused; no reference PDE was rerun. Density L1 differences from conservatively restricted Ny128 are.08431/.05802/.03503 and pressure differences.09556/.06798/.04156. Reference64/128 increments are.00955/.01250, about.273/.301 of the finest primary differences. Maximum relative four-component boundary-budget residual is about4.60e-13.

  • Same-problem reference · Finite-grid numerical reference

    Double Mach reflection: saved independent finite-grid numerical reference

    Compare against two previously independently executed finite-volume reference grids using conservative restriction. This is a finite-grid numerical reference, not an exact2D solution or error bound.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Nondimensional[0,4]x[0,1], gamma1.4, Mach10. Shock footx=1/6, angle60degrees; postshock(rho,u,v,p)=(8,8.25sqrt(3)/2,-4.125,116.5), upstream(1.4,0,0,1). Initial cells are classified by their centers, not exact cut-cell means. Left postshock inflow, right zero-gradient, bottom postshock forx<1/6 and slip wall otherwise; top postshock forx<1/6+(1+20t)/sqrt(3).

Editorial clarification

A lightweight comparison with an independent finite-grid numerical reference, not an exact2D full-field solution. Separate measured shock location, conservation budgets and wall-jet diagnostics from convergence of the thin wall jet. Forward-facing step is outside this execution scope.

Adopted numerical method

The published Numart piecewise-constant HLL flux, unsplit x/y divergence and Heun/SSPRK(2,2) form a small standalone package with both-stage boundary accounting and state checks. CFL.4 uses the sum of directional maximum acoustic rates; the top boundary uses each actual RK stage time. No state floor, repair or hidden retry. Invalid stages retain raw arrays/history and fail.

All21 tests, three final-time runs and40 gates passed with-W error. Verification limits and failures

The reference is finite-grid numerical data, not an exact2D solution or an Athena/LAVA execution. The HLL family is shared, but reference spatial operators are separately written and not imported by the primary. The reference increment is an uncertainty diagnostic, not an error bound. Initial projection, sampled moving boundaries, discretization and finite-reference effects all enter the difference; the slope is no rigorous order or full reflection-pattern convergence proof. The upper-front discrepancy stays2cells while its physical width shrinks. Fixed near-wall ROIx in[1,2.75],y<=.25 is not feature tracking. Finest ROI maxu12.644 versus reference16.125 shows the thin wall jet/roll-up is unresolved. Forward step, other wall data, general perturbations, higher order and full-pattern convergence are unverified.

Reference and validation scope

Inputs, acceptance,24 unit checks and numerical source were frozen before the first primary test/PDE execution. Checks cover analytic Mach3 normal-shock Rankine-Hugoniot identities, uniform parallel-channel flow, zero stationary-wall mass/energy flux, step-pressure force orientation, actual four-component budgets and raw failure retention. A reference revision removed only unnecessary diagnostic-string allocation and was repinned before first primary execution; physical inputs,arithmetic,CFL and acceptance values did not change. A lightweight verification on fixed inputs and a small number of grids. It does not establish agreement with the original corner-corrected PPM picture or convergence of fine slip lines and vortices.

Ordinary public-ZIP verification reads saved reference data; reference source, contracts and execution records are bundled. The first referenceNy160 exhausted its preregistered120second budget; that actual timeout is preserved. A reference revision removed only unnecessary diagnostic-string allocation and was repinned before first primary execution; physical inputs,arithmetic,CFL and acceptance values did not change. All24 tests, three final-time runs and45 gates passed with-W error. Primary density L1=.14754/.12878/.10265, pressure L1=.19373/.16015/.12242 and last-pair density slope=.327. Reference80/160 increments=.02636/.03063, about.257/.250 of the finest primary differences. Maximum four-component relative boundary-budget residual=2.99e-13; all integrated wall mass/energy fluxes are zero. The three primary grids took about46seconds on the original Mac; revised reference80/160 took about8/65seconds.

Verification limits and failures

The reference is separately implemented but shares the HLL family and Heun; no external AMROC,LAVA or RKDG engine was executed. Finite-grid numerical data are neither an exact2D solution nor an error bound. Without special corner treatment, a numerical entropy layer may be advected downstream; no agreement with corrected originalPPM fine structures is claimed. Whole-fluid differences,Linf and fixed corner density/pressure/entropy diagnostics are retained. Slopes do not prove pure spatial order; thin slip lines,roll-up,general geometries and high-order convergence remain unverified. Normalized maximum density differences=.592/.670/.665 do not decrease. Corner minima of log(p/rho^gamma)=-.0784/-.1224/-.3510 change substantially. This absolute entropy variable includes an arbitrary additive constant; a more-negative value is not itself an error increase. Neither stable corner extrema nor pointwise pattern convergence is established.

Stored measurements and decisions

Display values are rounded. Acceptance uses original fixed-input tolerances and unrounded numbers; only stored results passing every check are presented.

Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

  1. Paul Woodward and Phillip Colella (1984). The numerical simulation of two-dimensional fluid flow with strong shocks · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(84)90142-6

    Review scope / review_level: previously-reviewed-publisher-metadata; setup cross-checked against Cockburn-Shu1991 primary report

    Cited as the original standard strong-shock comparison. The publisher page rejected retrieval in this task; no direct full-paper reading is claimed. Setup and the distinction between corner treatments were checked in the primary Cockburn–Shu(1991) report.

  2. Bernardo Cockburn and Chi-Wang Shu (1991). The P¹-RKDG Method for Two-Dimensional Euler Equations of Gas Dynamics

    Review scope / review_level: selected-text-review: Example2 printedp7/PDFpage11 and Fig3 captions printedp8/PDFpage12

    Reviewed Example2 setup, Mach3 uniform flow, inlet/outlet/reflection boundaries, T4 and the Fig3 distinction between untreated and specially treated corners. Selected text only; no figure redistribution or RKDG execution.

  3. Ralf Deiterding / AMROC project (2004). 2D Euler equations — Forward facing step

    Review scope / review_level: official-example-selected-problem-description

    Checked the official example description explicitly omitting special corner entropy corrections and using T4. No AMROC calculation, AMR or figure is imported.

  4. Hiroshi Koyama (2026). Independent C++17 MUSCL finite-volume reference for the uncorrected Mach-3 forward-facing step

    Review scope / review_level: source-and-preregistered-new-execution

    Separate implementation without primary spatial-operator imports. HLL and Heun families are shared; no external engine execution. The original timeout and diagnostic-argument-only performance revision are retained alongside saved data,inputs,execution history and contracts.
